# Screenshot rules (house rules - unchanged; the toolkit does the pixel work)

## 3. Screenshot rules
- Never modify screenshot content unless told. No resizing: keep ORIGINAL size (the image width is set to 1250 px afterwards through the image properties - see section 8 - never by resizing the pixels). Only add the border and markings.
- REUSING OLD MANUAL IMAGES WITH A NEW MENU SCREENSHOT (ONLY when the user places the old images in the screenshots folder - never take images from an existing manual on your own, see section 0): when the user gives a new menu screenshot together with old manual images to reuse, first compare every reused image with the new menu screenshot and with any current screen the user gave: BL number, voyage / vessel, ports, customer, record values, screen layout, pop-up title and columns, which screen the result sits on (e.g. a success bar on a different module), and results that do not follow from the entered data (e.g. charges still showing the old exchange rate after revalidation). Report every discrepancy to the user as a numbered list and ask how to handle each one (edit the screenshot to match, or get a new screenshot) BEFORE marking. Never silently reuse a mismatching image.
- Grey side areas: before adding the border, crop away any grey area on the LEFT and RIGHT edges of every screenshot (browser/window shadow gradient, grey background strip, hatched grey background, dimmed background showing beside a pop-up, and blank padding beyond it). Crop only that grey area, never the app's own content, frame or buttons (e.g. keep a pop-up's close X). Do this for every image EXCEPT side-function screenshots (their side icons sit on the right edge). Crop before marking, so all box coordinates follow the cropped image.
- Blue border: white padding 18px, 2px #0066CC rounded rectangle (radius 12), 1px outer margin.
- Greyed-out screenshots (pop-up/alert over dimmed screen): fill the padding inside the border with grey #999999 instead of white (auto-detect: median brightness of the screenshot edge < 200, sampled a few pixels in from the edge so a 1-2 px white screen edge does not hide the dimming).
- Only screenshots in "How to" pages are marked. Overview pages use plain screenshots (except main/sub module images which keep their red tile box).
- Markings: 3px pure red (#FF0000) rectangle; numbered circle ~28px, white fill, 2px red outline, bold red number = step number (smaller font for 2-digit numbers so they fit inside the circle). Numbers continue across screenshots.
- Circle placement (as in the Import Documentation manual): the circle's centre sits exactly on its own box's line (edge or corner), half inside and half outside the box, never away from it. Take the FIRST spot in this order that covers no text, icon or other box:
  a. Buttons, icons, side icons, single checkboxes and radio buttons: middle of the LEFT edge (e.g. Apply in How to Update Credit Customer). Pad the box on the left so the circle clears the button's icon/text.
  b. Tall boxes (checkbox column, grid rows, Remarks box, a group of fields): LEFT edge, at the middle or just below it, clear of row text.
  c. One-line boxes whose left side sits against other content (menu items, radio options in a row, field boxes): BOTTOM-LEFT corner (e.g. the "Status Change" menu item and the "Close" radio option on the BL Status Change pages).
  d. Left side blocked (a sub-menu item next to its boxed parent menu item, a button with another button just to its left): mirror to the right - middle of the RIGHT edge for buttons and icons (e.g. Submit next to Fetch on the BL Print pages), BOTTOM-RIGHT corner for everything else (e.g. "BL Print" >> "BL Print" in the record menu).
  e. Only if all of these are blocked: TOP-LEFT corner, then TOP-RIGHT corner.
  Never use the middle of the top or bottom edge, and never put a circle on a line shared with another box. The ONLY exception is the two-box / one-number rule (query screens and pop-ups), which places its ONE number where the two boxes meet.
- Markings are drawn AFTER the blue border is added (offset every coordinate by 21px = 1px margin + 2px line + 18px padding), so a number may sit in the white/grey padding. A box touching the screenshot's edge therefore still takes its normal left-edge number.
- Boxes must never cut through text: enlarge the box to enclose the text (e.g. step 6 charge selection box encloses checkbox column + Charge column + BL row). A box may be unnumbered when it is just context (drop-down field) or when it illustrates a note rather than a step.
- Tiny icons (menu ☰ etc.): pad the box so the circle clears the icon.
- Inline crops (buttons, icons) are cut at original size from the user's screenshots. House icons come from the template's `_House Icons` topic, one per line in order: `select_all` (25x19), `single_select` (23x18), `batch_menu` (17x16), `record_menu`, `print` - decode the picture `screen_bits` (base64 PNG) on each line; the key is the text after the image.
- Before building, zoom into every marking and check nothing covers text.
- REUSING MARKED SCREENSHOTS (ON DEMAND ONLY - only when the user asks to clear/reuse a screenshot they placed in the screenshots folder, e.g. one taken from an existing manual or one that already has red boxes/numbers): 
  1. If it has the house blue border, strip it first (crop 21px from every side; older manuals use a 17px border).
  2. Remove all old markings: red/orange box lines (straight runs >= 25px), numbered red circles (red ring radius 10-17 with white inside, also when sitting on a box line), and short red line stubs left at box corners/ends. Fill the removed pixels by inpainting (cv2.INPAINT_TELEA). Never touch the app's own red UI (red menu icon, red text such as WB/TLX, red stars, close X, red status strips on rows - restore them from the original if removed).
  3. Zoom-check the cleaned image. Where an old number or box sat over text, a button or an icon, the spot can look smudged or a letter can be clipped. Fix each smudge in this order:
     a. If the new marking will cover it (the field/button gets a new box or number there), just mark over it - no repair needed.
     b. Otherwise rebuild it from a similar screenshot the user has given (same screen, unmarked at that spot - e.g. the earlier/later shot of the same screen, or another shot the user placed in the screenshots folder): match the area around the smudge in that screenshot and copy the clean pixels in (`python tools/ilis.py patch SRC DST --donor D --box B`; it only copies when the match score is >= 0.9). For a damaged button with no clean copy, rebuild its edge from the mirrored other edge or from a sibling button of the same style. Zoom-check the result.
     c. Only if neither works, tell the user which spots are still smudged and ask whether to keep them or get a clean screenshot.
  4. Then treat the clean image like any new screenshot: re-mark it with the current rules (border first, then boxes/numbers with the current step numbers).
- EDITING SCREENSHOT CONTENT (ON DEMAND ONLY - when the user asks to change a record, value, label or message in a screenshot): rebuild text from glyphs of the same font found in the same or a sibling screenshot (same colour and background; remap antialiasing when the background differs), keep spacing consistent, and zoom-check. Render text with a font (Liberation Sans Bold ~10.75px for the green success bar) only when no glyph source exists. Show the edited images as a preview for confirmation.
- SWAPPING THE SCREEN TITLE (ON DEMAND ONLY - when a function was renamed and the user gives an old screenshot plus a crop of the new title tab, e.g. "Collect Charge" -> "Local Charge"): keep the old screenshot exactly as it is (grid, data and any existing boxes/numbers untouched) and replace only the title tab with the new crop (do it as a recipe: `copy_region` of the title-tab crop with `align: none` and an `offset`, see toolkit.md).
  1. Flatten both images onto white (no transparent pixels).
  2. Align the crop by anchors that appear in both: the left edge of the dark "Import Activity" text (x) and the tab underline / the light-blue separator line under the tabs (y). The offset must agree on both lines.
  3. Fill the old title area with white (wide enough to cover the old tab, its X and its underline; stop above the separator line), then paste the crop at the offset. Drop any edge row of the crop that carries a stray separator line or screenshot edge.
  4. Zoom-check the seam (2x crop of the top-left corner): the new tab should sit on the same baseline, the underline and pointer in line, the separator line unbroken, the blue border intact. Then show the preview (name it f_<function>_sample.png or as the page needs).
- ASKING ABOUT BOX PLACEMENT: never ask in words only (e.g. "should the box cover section X or section Y too?"). Always generate the marked option images (Option A / B / C, fully marked with boxes, numbers and border, each with the step numbering it implies), show them as one preview sheet (`preview`), and ask the user to pick one.


## Added rules (from the user, November 2026)
1. BUILDING MISSING SCREENSHOTS: screenshots are mostly new, but when a flow is incomplete, build the missing image from neighbouring or matchable screenshots (same flow, or elsewhere in the manual). Example: given the Release Order screen and an alert like "Release Order Print done Successfully.", create the "Release Order Cancelled Successfully." alert over that screen with the message the user gives (recipe `alert_from_screen`). Same for pop-up texts (`popup_text`), success messages (`success_bar`), records changed after processing (`change_value`), and regions from a neighbour shot (`copy_from_neighbour`).
   - When looking for a screenshot to build from, search in this order: (1) the same function's folder, (2) other function folders in the same section (Batch Function / Single Function / Side Functions), (3) any other folder in screenshots. Always say which file you used. If nothing matches, ask the user for the image and name the step.
2. If there is no image to build from and the flow is not complete, ASK the user for the missing image, naming the step it is for.
3. PREVIEW EVERY EDITED IMAGE: whenever an image is edited or built, show its preview right away so the user can correct it there, before it goes into a page.
4. CROP BUTTONS BEFORE MARKING: inline button/icon crops are always cut from the unmarked screenshot, before any box or number is drawn.
